title: Purity of smooth proper cohomology
statement:
Fix the finite-field datum
$(p,a,q,k_0,k)$, where $q=p^a$, and a prime $\ell\neq p$; write
$\Ql=\mathbf Q_\ell$, choose an algebraic closure $\Qlb$ of $\Ql$,
fix an isomorphism $\iota:\Qlb\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathbf C$, and interpret
the $\Qlb$-objects in the
algebraically closed
coefficient category. Let $X_0/k_0$ be
smooth, proper, geometrically
connected of pure dimension $d\in\mathbf Z_{\geq0}$, put
$X=X_0\times_{k_0}k$, let $F$ be the
global geometric Frobenius
in the geometric-Frobenius convention, and
let $(\Qlb)_X$ be the constant
$\Qlb$-sheaf on
$X$; no admissibility hypothesis is imposed on the structure morphism
$a_X:X_0\to\Spec k_0$ (its exceptional inverse image is the constructible
one, defined for every separated finite-type morphism; the ambient notion of
[def-weil-exceptional-adjoint-admissibility] is not used). Then, for every $i\in\mathbf Z$, the Frobenius module

$$
(H^i(X,\Qlb),F)
$$

is $\iota$-pure of weight $i$ in the sense of
[def-weil-frobenius-module-weights]; the group
$H_c^i(X,\Qlb)=H^i(X,\Qlb)$ (proper coincidence,
[prop-weil-operations]) is $\iota$-mixed of weights at most $i$.

proof.text: Set $Y_0=\operatorname{Spec}k_0$ and let $a_0:X_0\to Y_0$ be the structure morphism. The finite-field and geometric conventions [def-weil-finite-field-fiber, def-weil-geometric-hypotheses] identify its geometric fibre with $X$; it is smooth and proper with pure relative dimension $d$, exactly the hypotheses of the relative theorem. Take the constant sheaf $\mathcal F_0=(\Qlb)_{X_0}$ with its canonical Weil structure [def-weil-constant-weil-structure]. It is lisse in [def-pod-lisse-l-adic-sheaves]: at $E=\Ql$ use the constant rank-one systems $A_{E,n}$, whose reduction maps satisfy $A_{E,n+1}\otimes_{A_{E,n+1}}A_{E,n}=A_{E,n}$; rationalize and then take the pair at that finite coefficient stage. Thus the lisse condition requires no geometric trivialization beyond the identity cover. The coefficient object used here is the completed integral unit and its scalar extensions, not the discrete constant sheaf of the infinite field: [lem-weil-constant-coefficient-objects-constructible], clauses (2)–(3), identifies its derived reductions with the finite constant coefficient sheaves and its rational image with the common-stage pair. These are the constant finite systems just displayed (constant finite sheaves remain constant under the site inverse image), so this supplies the required coefficient realization of the lisse constant object.

source.place: Proof, first paragraph: choice of base, morphism and constant lisse sheaf

proof.text: By [lem-zl-constant-sheaf-weight-zero], $\mathcal F_0$ is punctually $\iota$-pure of weight $0$. Apply [prop-zl-smooth-proper-relative-purity] with $f_0=a_0$, $w=0$. Its last paragraph explicitly states the absolute constant-coefficient conclusion: every eigenvalue $\alpha$ of geometric Frobenius on $H^i(X,\Qlb)$ satisfies $|\iota(\alpha)|=q^{i/2}$. Here the sole closed point of $Y_0$ has residue field $k_0$, degree $1$ and $q_y=q$; the fibre is $X$. Thus the absolute clause uses exactly the global geometric Frobenius $F$ fixed in the statement. Clause (a) also puts the direct-image sheaf in the lisse constructible category. The point-fibre/cohomology convention [def-weil-ordinary-compact-cohomology] takes these coefficient complexes to $D^b_{\mathrm{fd}}(\Qlb)$, so the cohomology spaces are finite-dimensional. The global operator [def-weil-global-geometric-frobenius] is the cohomology action of the displayed transport isomorphism followed by the Weil isomorphism, hence is invertible. Therefore these are Frobenius modules, and the eigenvalue equality is precisely purity of weight $i$ under [def-weil-frobenius-module-weights].

source.place: Proof, first paragraph (weight zero) and second paragraph through purity

proof.text: The structure morphism $a_X:X\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ is the base change of the proper $a_0$ along $\operatorname{Spec}k\to\operatorname{Spec}k_0$, so it is proper by [lem-weil-pbc-proper-base-change]. Apply [prop-weil-proper-compact-coincidence] to its geometric fibre $X$ and constant coefficient object: $Ra_{X!}\cong Ra_{X*}$, and hence $H_c^i(X,\Qlb)\cong H^i(X,\Qlb)$. Equivariance is supplied by [prop-weil-operations], whose statement makes these comparison isomorphisms morphisms of Weil complexes and the induced cohomology maps Frobenius-equivariant. Equivalently, the isomorphism of Weil sheaves in clause (a) of [prop-zl-smooth-proper-relative-purity] at $a_0$ gives this same comparison after taking the geometric fibre over the unique point of $\operatorname{Spec}k_0$. Thus the proper-coincidence identification in the conclusion preserves the Frobenius operators.

source.place: Proof, second paragraph: proper coincidence and Frobenius equivariance

proof.text: Write $V=H_c^i(X,\Qlb)$ and identify it with $H^i(X,\Qlb)$ by Step 3. Its eigenvalues are the same: an equivariant isomorphism sends a nonzero $\alpha$-eigenvector to a nonzero $\alpha$-eigenvector, and its inverse does the converse. Hence Step 2 makes $V$ pure of weight $i$. In the mixedness definition [def-weil-frobenius-module-weights], take $m=1$, $V_0=0$, $V_1=V$ and $w_1=i$. This is an $F$-stable filtration and its sole quotient is $V$; $w_1\leq i$. It proves mixedness of weights at most $i$. If $V=0$ the same filtration is allowed (its inclusions need not be strict), or one can take $m=0$. All steps hold for every integer $i$ and $d\geq0$; zero cohomology has no eigenvalues, so its purity condition is vacuous.

source.place: Proof, second paragraph, final sentence: pure implies mixed
